definitions.explanation: The whitish mineral deposit left by hot water inside kettles, pots, bathtubs, and water heaters. Also used for the film that builds up on the inside of a bath.

examples.japanese: やかんに{湯垢|ゆあか}がついた。
examples.english: Scale has built up in the kettle.

examples.japanese: {風呂|ふろ}の{湯垢|ゆあか}をこすって{落|お}とす。
examples.english: I scrub off the scum in the bathtub.

examples.japanese: {湯垢|ゆあか}はクエン{酸|さん}を{使|つか}うときれいに{取|と}れる。
examples.english: Limescale comes off nicely if you use citric acid.

examples.japanese: {毎日|まいにち}{洗|あら}っていても、{浴槽|よくそう}には{少|すこ}しずつ{湯垢|ゆあか}がたまっていく。
examples.english: Even if you wash it every day, scum gradually builds up in the bathtub.

notes:
Formed from {湯|ゆ} (hot water) + {垢|あか} (grime, dirt). It refers to deposits left by the water itself, mostly minerals, rather than to body dirt.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {湯垢|ゆあか}がつく: scale forms
- {湯垢|ゆあか}がたまる: scale builds up
- {湯垢|ゆあか}を{落|お}とす: to remove scale
- {湯垢|ゆあか}{取|と}り: scale remover (product)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {水垢|みずあか}: water stains — the same kind of deposit left by cold water, on sinks and faucets
- {垢|あか}: grime — the general word, including dirt from the skin
